body.p: A pointer may also hold the address of a procedure or a function. Such a pointer declares the complete signature of the routine it can point at, and calls through it look like ordinary calls.

section.title: Declaring a callable pointer
section.codeblock:
VAR POINTER handler AS PROCEDURE (BYTE IN) VAR POINTER setter AS PROCEDURE (BYTE OUT) VAR POINTER bumper AS PROCEDURE (BYTE IN OUT) VAR POINTER calc AS FUNCTION (BYTE IN) RETURN WORD
VAR POINTER handlers[4] AS PROCEDURE (BYTE IN) VAR POINTER calcs[4] AS FUNCTION (BYTE IN, BYTE IN) RETURN BYTE
section.p: The signature must match the routine exactly: the same number of parameters, the same parameter directions, and the same return type. A mismatch is a compile error.

section.title: Binding and calling
section.codeblock:
PROCEDURE log(BYTE IN value) IS ... END PROCEDURE FUNCTION double(BYTE IN value) RETURN WORD IS ... END FUNCTION
VAR POINTER handler AS PROCEDURE (BYTE IN) VAR POINTER calc AS FUNCTION (BYTE IN) RETURN WORD VAR WORD result
handler IS log calc IS double
handler(42) -- calls log result = calc(21) -- calls double, result = 42
section.p: Every parameter direction works through a pointer call. An OUT or IN OUT actual is marshalled back into the caller's variable after the call returns, so the call site cannot tell a pointer call from a direct call:
section.codeblock:
PROCEDURE set(BYTE OUT value) IS value = 21 END PROCEDURE PROCEDURE bump(BYTE IN OUT value) IS value = value + 1 END PROCEDURE
VAR POINTER sp AS PROCEDURE (BYTE OUT) VAR POINTER bp AS PROCEDURE (BYTE IN OUT) VAR BYTE victim VAR BYTE counter = 25
sp IS set sp(victim) -- victim = 21
bp IS bump bp(counter) -- counter = 26

section.title: Pointer slots
section.p: An array of callable pointers holds several routines that share one signature. Slots are bound with IS and called with a constant or a runtime index:
section.codeblock:
PROCEDURE proc_c(BYTE IN test) IS ... END PROCEDURE PROCEDURE proc_d(BYTE IN test) IS ... END PROCEDURE
VAR POINTER proc_slots[2] AS PROCEDURE (BYTE IN) VAR BYTE step = 0
proc_slots[0] IS proc_c proc_slots[1] IS proc_d
WHILE step < 2 LOOP proc_slots[step](0) -- dispatch by runtime index step = step + 1 END LOOP
section.p: WHEREIS works on an indexed slot and reports the address of the routine it is bound to, or zero when the slot is unbound.

section.title: Return values
section.p: A scalar procedure pointer is called exactly like the procedure it points at. A function pointer is called wherever a value is expected. The return value of a function call may also be ignored: calling a function as a statement is legal and discards the result without an error or a warning. This applies to direct calls, pointer calls, and pseudo-variable 'get calls.
